steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C ). Put butter into a 2-quart casserole dish and place into the oven to melt while preheating.
When butter melts, remove the casserole dish from the oven. Mix both types of corn, cornbread mix, and sour cream into melted butter until well combined.
Bake in the preheated oven for about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Corn Pudding
raw_recipe.description: This easy corn pudding is perfect for the holidays and only requires 5 ingredients: cornbread mix, two types of canned corn, butter, and sour cream.

video.description: My father-in-law was always a picky eater. However, the first Thanksgiving I made him this recipe, he went crazy! It soon became a tradition, and now he is gone, it is always mentioned as one of his favorites.
video.name: How to Make Easy Corn Pudding

review.reviewBody: The first time I made this recipe I added two eggs like other reviewers suggested and it was fabulous. The second time I made it (this time for a crowd) I forgot to add the second egg, but it was still delicious. When I make it again I will add the second egg though; it was better.

Loved it and so did everyone in the crowd. I added 2 eggs, and didn't drain the corn. The 2nd time I cut the butter down to 1/3 cup and still it was great. Tried it both with and without the sour cream and liked it both ways -- with the sour cream it was softer, creamier consistency, without it was a little more bread-like.

I didn't grow up with this, but a friend who often invited me to Thanksgiving when I lived in NYC made it. I've been craving it lately. It was similar to hers and the scoop of corn cake served at Chevy's. I made a double batch, which filled a 9x13 dish, plus two ~6" ramekins. I baked the ramekins on a baking sheet for about 45 minutes. I turned the oven off and left the 9x13" pan in. The sides were brown, similar to baked stuffing. The tops were not crusted, except one I put cheese on. I used what I had on hand: 2 Jiffy corn muffin mixes, 15 oz can creamed corn, 30 oz can whole kernel corn (that's 15 oz less than called for, but it was plenty of corn), 3 eggs, about 8 oz of a 10 oz can of condensed cheddar cheese soup (sub for sour cream), 1.5 C sugar, the melted butter (1 stick, forgot to dbl), 1 C shredded cheddar cheese, and half the juice from the corn. I wasn't sure if the juice would be too much, so I strained it first. It was about a cup total, so I used about 1/2 C. I eyeballed it, assuming it should be thinner than cornbread/muffins batter. If you like it dense, you would not want both the corn juice & 2 eggs. At first, I was disappointed it was too thick, but it was perfect: dense, but soft, and creamy. Couldn't taste the cheese, except on top of the one ramekin, so I don't know how much difference it made to the taste or texture. Could have used 1 cup of sugar, it was about as sweet as Chevy's. It's amazing. I'm glad I made enough to freeze!

I made a version of this...had to tweak it some mostly based on ingredients I had and some food allergies in my family. I used frozen corn but blended 1/2 of it (to "cream it") with Emerson blender with Greek yogurt (instead of sour cream), 2 eggs (I used egg substitute), and added 1 small box of instant vanilla pudding mix and 1/2cup milk...whole family enjoyed

I have made this three times using the recommended 350 degree oven at 30 minutes. Every time, at 30 minutes, it was still soupy. It took almost 90 minutes for the top to crisp. I will now cook it at 375 degrees for an hour. The first time I used it, I used Jiffy. It didn't taste great. So, now I use whole sweet Corn, Kerrygold Pure Irish Butter, and Famous Dave's Original Corn Bread Mix. The flavors make such a difference.

Delicious!! I scrolled through the recipe before making it and my first thought was 'No eggs?' Soooo I read through the reviews and chose to add two eggs, a little salt and a little pepper and the optional sourcream...my oven's really wonky so I erred on the side of caution and gave this 40 minutes at 350 and it was wonderful!!!

Upped the heat to 375* and used a gluten free cornbread mix! Also used Sweet Corn Soup by Natural Grocers since they didn’t have any creamed corn (It comes in a 14 oz bag. If they hadn’t had the soup, I would have just put about half a can of corn in my Nutrabullet , blended, then add the rest of corn). It was amazing!! I’m making it again right now. Definitely going into the family cookbook of favorite recipes!

This has been a favorite in our family every year for at least the last 7-8 years. I always double the recipe, add eggs (2 eggs x2 for doubling, stay with one stick of butter instead of doubling and I drain one of the whole corn kernels liquid and keep the liquid from the 2nd can. I also use sour cream. Bake for 45ish minutes. Thanks to several others before me for all their suggestions that have made it perfect!

I didn't have any sour cream. I was going to use plain Greek yogurt but didn't have that either. I added the 2 eggs made a double batch. Drained one can of the whole kernel corn. Used the liquid from the 2nd one, heated it on the stove, added 3 teaspoons of corn starch to the hot liquid. Only added 1 can of the creamed style.

This was my first time making it, so I took lots of advice from other reviewers. I doubled the recipe and added three eggs, didn't drain the corn, mixed the melted butter in, and added a little shredded cheese. I pre-cooked it about 35 minutes the night before, then cooked it about 45 minutes the day of. It was a big hit. Will definitely do this one again.
Prepared as written it tastes good. The second time I made it I added another egg and 1/2 cup finely shredded cheddar. That brought it up to 5 stars in my book.
Awesome Easy 8g Protein per serving !
Very good a great find for the Holidays

As a southern man taught to cook by his grandmother. It needs more sugar. Lemon extract. Vanilla extract. No cornbread mix.. half cup of flour and nutmeg and cinnamon... and evaporated milk... whatever recipe this is above is horrible. Its like cornbread..
Excellent & so easy to make. It tastes so wonderful !!!
A bit heavy on the butter (don’t need to use that much). Also, this always takes double the cooking time (longer if you’re doubling the recipe)

This was my first making this casserole. Absolutely delicious! It was slightly sweet and creamy! Very light! Next time, I will use half and half to increase richness. A nice accompaniment to my pork chop dinner!
I love this and it is a new family favorite. Sometimes when I double the recipe, I replace half of the sour cream with ricotta cheese.
Easy and tasty!
